name: Long bar display
look: a long low desk display with soft rounded corners, a slim bar screen on the left and a round touch button on the right
picture_prompt: Product concept render of a small 3D-printable desk device, seen from the front and slightly to one side. It is about three times as wide as it is tall. One smooth continuous body with soft rounded corners. On the left of the front is a long flat bar screen, about 55 mm wide and 15 mm tall, in a slim even bezel. On the right of the front is one shallow round dimple about 12 mm across, used as a touch button, with no knobs. One matte plastic colour with a dark screen. Soft studio light, plain light background. Flat bottom, flat back, no text, no logos, no speaker holes, no feet, no visible seams, no cables.
sheet: Front faces -y and stands upright. World +z is up.
Left about 70% of the front: the bar screen, landscape, with its long side along x, a separate board just behind the front wall.
Right about 30% of the front: the touch sensor, flat behind the front wall, reached through a round opening in a shallow dimple. Its pins point into the case, toward +y.

The controller is a long separate board behind the screen, with its long side along x, so its USB reaches the left wall. Its top faces the back (+y) and its pins point forward (-y), with their plugs between it and the screen.

Build it from the back, in this order, each part coming in from +y: PRINT_Shell first, lying face down; then the screen; then the touch sensor; then PRINT_Carrier holding the controller; then PRINT_Base last. Nothing on the Shell may have to pass the screen to reach the controller.
The Carrier stops the controller toward the front. A rib on PRINT_Base stops it toward the back.
USB opens on the left side (-x).
The wires run behind the screen board as one neat bundle, side by side, and do not show from outside.
The seam is a flat plane near the back, so from the front the Shell looks like one continuous body and the Base is only a rear cover.
